author: NASASpaceflight
description:
Can a new mission keep Hubble exploring the universe? NASA is asking industry about options to reboost, service, or safely deorbit the iconic space telescope—and Jared Isaacman shares his thoughts on its future.

In this episode of This Week in Spaceflight, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman also joins NSF to discuss Artemis III, Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander, SpaceX’s Starship, the future of SLS and Orion, and the transition from the International Space Station to commercial destinations.

Plus, Rocket Lab moves major Neutron hardware to Wallops for testing, Virgin Galactic reveals its first Delta-class spaceship, Apeiron, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory discovers a new dwarf planet candidate beyond Neptune.

Also in this week’s update:
• ESA’s Hera spacecraft gets a clearer look at Didymos and Dimorphos
• NASA’s ultraviolet survey telescope UVEX moves forward
• Blue Origin advances New Glenn testing and launch pad repairs
• ULA prepares Vulcan for its return to flight
